title: Rotate with stack and index
starter:
%a = param [] slot=0 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%b = param [] slot=1 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%c = param [] slot=2 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%i = param [] slot=3 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%out = add %a 0
hints: `stack` turns your three scalars into one rank-1 value, and `index` reads one element back out.
The element after position `i` is at position `i + 1`, wrapped back into 0, 1, 2 with `mod`.

`mod` keeps the sign of the dividend, so `mod (i + 1) 3` is negative when `i + 1` is (try `i = -2` and `i = INT_MAX`, where `i + 1` wraps to `INT_MIN`). Add 3 and take `mod 3` again to land in 0, 1, 2.
prompt: Params a, b, c and i are i32. Stack a b c. Compute j = i + 1 with i32 add (so INT_MAX + 1 wraps), and return the element at j mod 3. i = 2 gives a. Because mod floors, j mod 3 is always 0, 1 or 2, even for a negative j, and its bounds say so: that's what makes the index valid.

answer.code:
%a = param [] slot=0 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%b = param [] slot=1 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%c = param [] slot=2 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%i = param [] slot=3 dtype=i32 addrspace=ALU
%s = stack %a %b %c
%j = add %i 1
%k = mod %j 3
%out = index %s %k
answer.explain: The reference stacks `a b c`, computes `(i + 1) mod 3`, then adds 3 and takes `mod 3` again. C-style `mod` can return -1 or -2 when `i + 1` is negative (including when `i = INT_MAX` wraps to `INT_MIN`), and the second `mod` folds that back into `[0, 2]`, which is what the bounds-checked `index` needs.
